verses.text: The Amorite kings west of the Jordan and the Canaanite kings along the coast heard how the LORD had dried up the Jordan in front of the Israelites until we crossed. They lost heart, and there was no courage left in them to face Israel.
At that time the LORD told Joshua, “Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelite men again. This will be the second time.”
Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelite men at the Hill of the Foreskins.
Here's why Joshua circumcised them. The men of fighting age who came out of Egypt had all died along the way in the wilderness after leaving Egypt.
All those who came out had been circumcised, but those born in the wilderness on the journey from Egypt hadn't been circumcised.

The Israelites traveled through the wilderness for forty years until all the fighting men who had come out of Egypt died, because they hadn't listened to the LORD. He swore they wouldn't see the land he had sworn to give our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.
The LORD raised up their children in their place. Joshua circumcised them, because they hadn't been circumcised along the way.
When the whole nation had finished with the circumcision, everyone stayed where they were in camp until they healed.
The LORD told Joshua, “Today I've rolled away the shame of Egypt from you.” That's why the place is still called Gilgal today.
The Israelites camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho. There they kept the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month.
The very next day after Passover they ate food grown in the land: flatbread made without yeast and roasted grain.
The day after they ate the land's produce, the manna stopped. The Israelites didn't get manna anymore. That year they ate food from the land of Canaan.
When Joshua was near Jericho he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword. Joshua walked over and asked him, “Are you on our side or our enemies' side?”
“Neither,” he said. “I've come as commander of the LORD's army.” Joshua fell facedown, bowed in worship, and asked, “What does my lord have to say to his servant?”
The commander of the LORD's army told Joshua, “Take off your sandals. The place you're standing on is holy.” So Joshua took them off.
